# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).

## Architecture

- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).

## Portals & design system

**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.

- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).

- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).

- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.

- Design system tokens/classes live in `app/globals.css` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (shared/production) and `components/nx/*` (Nexion-only). Charts are dependency-free SVG (`components/ui/charts.tsx`) — do not add a charting library.
- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners). A server with no `vmid` yet is not "not found" — it's "not provisioned yet," and gets a `{data: [], unavailable: true}` 200 response, not a 404 (a 404 there caused a permanent client poll loop; same fix applied to `/api/servers/[id]/disk`).

## Working on this codebase — one tree, any session

`/opt/nxeon` (this directory, branch `main`) is the single source of truth. There is no longer a required separate sandbox for ordinary changes — the node-2 box (`/opt/nxeon-v2`) that incubated the Nexion redesign still exists and is safe to use for a large, risky, or highly iterative piece of work (it runs sandboxed: `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` stubs Proxmox provisioning and Stripe charges), but is optional, not a gate. Any session — this one or another — can edit `main` directly and ship through the pipeline below.

1. Edit, then `npx tsc --noEmit` before building anything.
2. `npm run build` locally only to catch build errors before pushing — do not restart production services from an ad hoc build in this directory (see Commands below); this is validation, not deployment.
3. Commit (small, real commits — the GitHub post-commit hook auto-pushes `origin`).
4. `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>` — builds, migrates, and restarts staging (`:8080`) from that ref. **Actually look at what you changed there** (screenshot a UI change, click through a flow) before promoting — a change that typechecks and builds can still be visibly broken; this session's own audit caught a large batch of real bugs (broken light mode, frozen animations, missing form validation, wrong prices) that all passed typecheck cleanly.
5. `scripts/promote-production.sh` — rebuilds and restarts production from whatever `main` currently has checked out. It refuses to run if staging isn't healthy first.

If two sessions are likely to be editing at once, coordinate the ordinary way: pull before starting, small commits, push often (the auto-push hook does this for you on commit).

## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)

- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id). Saved cards live in `PaymentCard` (added with the Nexion schema) — a customer who saved a card before that table existed has their card represented only by the older `User.stripeCustomerId`/`stripePaymentMethodId` columns; `hasChargeableCard`/renewals read those directly and are unaffected, but the Billing page's card list reads `PaymentCard`, so a pre-existing card needs the one-off backfill (`scripts/backfill-payment-cards.ts`) to show up there. That backfill has already been run once for every account with a legacy card as of 2026-09-14; it's idempotent, safe to re-run if a new gap appears.
- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.

## Conventions

- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
- Never fabricate: no invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, or ETAs. If a number can't be read from the database or a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why — this tree has had hash-derived star ratings and fake reviews removed once already.
- Minecraft subdomains (`*.play.nxeon.cloud`) are shared across two tables — `FreeMinecraftServer.subdomain` and `Server.subdomain` — because both products resolve under the same DNS zone. Always check availability through `lib/game-subdomain.ts`'s `isSubdomainAvailable()` (queries both) rather than checking either table alone, or a free and a paid server can claim the same name.

## Documentation — keep it current (required)

- **Every change, fix, or addition MUST update `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` in the same commit.** Add a dated bullet to §15 (Change history) and edit any section the change affects (data model, subsystems, feature catalog, integrations, roadmap, etc.). A commit that changes behaviour without touching the docs is incomplete.
- Keep `ROADMAP.md` in sync too: check off / move the item you completed.
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` is the single source of truth. The public mirror at `https://revsports.ca/docs` is regenerated from it with `node scripts/publish-docs.mjs` (zero-dep markdown→styled-HTML renderer → `/var/www/nxeon-docs/index.html`) — run that after editing the doc so the hosted page matches. The `/docs` nginx location lives in `scripts/configure-domains.sh` so it survives vhost regeneration.
- The claude.ai artifact webpage (`https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b0c97f5-4c34-4f89-bee9-b5a80eb23892`) can only be updated from an interactive Claude Code session (headless/cron runs can't reach it) — that refresh is best-effort, the repo doc + `/docs` page are authoritative.

## Commands

- Typecheck: `npx tsc --noEmit` (always, before a build)
- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — or, preferably, go through `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` → verify → `scripts/promote-production.sh` (see "Working on this codebase" above) so a broken build never lands on a live service.

# 05 Bridge and accounts

How a Nxeon customer becomes a Cyrus user, how money and plans move, and how Cyrus touches a customer's game server. State: **built and tested on node-2 with fakes and real Test Flight servers; nothing deployed; every switch OFF** (see [reference/flags-and-env.md](reference/flags-and-env.md), launch order in [07 operations](07-operations.md)).

## Today (inside Nxeon) vs the target
Today Cyrus uses Nxeon's sign-in, wallet, Stripe and game-server install path directly (through the host seam, [01 architecture](01-architecture.md)). The target (defaults from the full plan, 2026-10-11): **Nxeon is the identity provider and the only money system; Cyrus sells nothing itself**; per-server scoped grants, never SSH credentials; a separate Cyrus Postgres; Cyrus has its own admin; separate Cyrus Terms/Privacy (lawyer-reviewed before public launch). These are the working defaults agents r37-r40 built to (the owner was asked to confirm them in the full plan and has not objected); the open exceptions are in [12 gaps and roadmap](12-gaps-and-roadmap.md).

## SSO and identity (r36)
One app serves both hosts. `lib/cyrus/bridge/{config,routing}.ts` + middleware: cyrus.my gets the Cyrus brand bar around the same `/dashboard/cyrus` pages; the customer-app tree is exposed as `/home`, `/new`, `/account`, `/projects[/<id>]`; portal pages hand off to Nxeon; everything else 404s. **Sign in with Nxeon** = redirect with an Ed25519 signed assertion (state/nonce bound to the starting browser, single-use jti, exact `redirect_uri`, 120 s), a stable **subject id (Nxeon user id; never email)**, verified email required, a separate Cyrus cookie parented to the Nxeon session; **Sign in with Cyrus** on Nxeon lands on the same account; sign-up goes through Nxeon `/register` behind a consent screen; impersonation never crosses hosts; logout is a signed hop both ways. Keys: `CYRUS_BRIDGE_*` (secrets, env only). Routes under `/cyrus-host/*` (sign-in, sign-up, auth start/callback/handoff/lo
Verified: two-origin e2e 46/46 with the mode on and 6/6 off (no studio on cyrus.my, no IdP, internal tree 404, spoofed marker ignored); own-flow security review (open redirect, login CSRF, replay, forged subject, header spoofing, impersonation leak, fixation, consent/logout CSRF). Not run: `next build`, a real browser, staging behind nginx.

## Wallet, tokens and plans
- **Unit and sources**: see [00 overview](00-overview.md). 1 token = $0.002 of measured AI cost (`cyrus_tok_tokens_per_usd=500`), Yakko x1.25, min 5 per build. Game-server purchase grants `clamp(round5(100 + 16 x monthly $), 150, 750)`; each paid renewal `clamp(round5(25 + 6 x monthly $), 40, 300)` (only for games Cyrus builds for); lots expire after 90 days; plans Katara $4.99 = 750/month, Saka $19.99 = 3,500, All models $49.99 = 10,000, stacking, each month's tokens last 3 months; top-ups $5-$100 at 120 tokens/$, 12-month expiry. # 07 Operations

Authoritative step lists live in the repo runbooks: [CYRUS-DEPLOY-RUNBOOK.md](../CYRUS-DEPLOY-RUNBOOK.md) (owner, step by step), [CYRUS-TEST-DEPLOY.md](../CYRUS-TEST-DEPLOY.md) (release candidate rc1: the owner-only texture/sound/item-model/designer test on his own server, rehearsed), [CYRUS-MOVE-RUNBOOK.md](../CYRUS-MOVE-RUNBOOK.md) (move day, draft), [CYRUS-PLATFORM.md](../CYRUS-PLATFORM.md) (monorepo, ship, Cloudflare, data split, observability). This page is the summary, the infrastructure map and the incident playbooks. **Agents never deploy, run production migrations, flip flags or touch VM 88001 or customer servers; the owner does (classifier blocks prod deploys for agents).** Secrets are never in these docs: this page names where they live.

## Where things run
| Place | What | Notes |
|---|---|---|

| **node-2** (nxeon-fsn1, Germany) | the BUILD HOST: release builds, all agent dev work (`scripts/devhost`), Test Flight, meshgen/Blender sandbox, sound render, Try It controller, throwaway Postgres (port 5433) | Also runs about 13 customer VMs (never touch). Caps: slice `nxeon-build.slice` (CPUQuota 900%), agents slice memory raised 2026-10-10 to **10 GB** and the build slice to **13 GB** (older text in `/root/agent-notes/BUILD-HOST.md` says 7/10 GB); nice 10; **one heavy job at a time** via the lock `/run/lock/nxeon-build.lock`; locked agent jobs capped at 25 min. |
| **VM 88001** (Docker, inside the Nxeon network) | the build service image `modbuilder:<tag>` (Claude CLI + JDKs + classpaths) | Reached through the primary with a jump host. Running tag per last deploy: 0.4. Deploy only with `scripts/cyrus/deploy-modbuilder.sh` (derived from the Dockerfile, hash-checked, auto-rollback; `--list` first). |
| **Tank** (`/tank`) | one 3.6 TB spinning disk, NO redundancy: backups (689 GB), NX Labs mirror (150 GB quota), library staging, uploads, dev worktrees | Give the library its own dataset with a quota; keep a second copy of the proprietary SFX (owner OK pending). The NVMe pool is for customer VMs only. |
| Cloudflare | zone `cyrus.my` ACTIVE: apex + www proxied, served by nginx on the primary (`/etc/nginx/sites-enabled/cyrus-my`, root `/var/www/cyrus.my`); Nxeon zones NOT proxied yet | The Cloudflare API token that issued the certificate was pasted in chat once: **rotate it** (owner action). The token file path is `/root/.secrets/cloudflare-cyrus.ini` (root-only; never print). It cannot edit zone SSL settings: set SSL/TLS to **Full (strict)** in the dashboard. |

### cyrus.my hosting and the certificate watcher
Landing is a static site published atomically from `apps/cyrus-site` (`publish.sh`: release dirs, symlink swap, health check, auto-rollback, dry run unless `--go`; legacy dir kept as rollback). The Let's Encrypt certificate (DNS-01 via Cloudflare) was issued by the watcher `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-my-finish.sh` (log `cyrus-my-finish.log`: "cyrus.my now uses the Let's Encrypt cert"). Renewal is certbot's timer; check it after any nginx change. DNS for `app.`, `admin.`, `api.` subdomains and the nginx proxy paths are not done (owner list in OWNER-ACTIONS "r36").

## Deploy runbook (summary of the 8 steps, owner executes, one at a time, smoke after each)
Hazards first: never build or edit in `/opt/nxeon` (a raw build + restart caused two outages on 2026-10-01); check `uptime` first (the promote cutover rolls itself back on an overloaded primary); after stopping staging promote needs `--skip-staging-check`; never `pkill -f`; the 100+ commit branch is merged to `main` through a reviewed PR; every feature is OFF so landing the code changes nothing.
1. **Database**: additive manual SQL by hand, then check (`prisma/manual-migrations/*cyrus*.sql`, listed in [reference/db-tables.md](reference/db-tables.md); engine core has a trigger that must be run by hand; `scripts/cyrus-seed-managed-plugins.ts` after managed plugins).
2. **Code to production** with all switches off: `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>`, look at it, then `scripts/promote-production.sh`.
3. **Rebuild the build-service image on VM 88001** (`deploy-modbuilder.sh`, `JDK25=yes` for the 26.x lane; verifies `promptVersion`, `features.catalogTools`, `release.scannerSha256` = sha256 of `scan.js`, `release.registrySha256`; sends one injection-style request that must be refused).
4. **Switch the build service from the subscription login to an API key** before ANY public launch (`/health` field `auth` must read `api_key`; subscription login cannot power a public service).
5. **Infrastructure the switches depend on**: pack storage + public base, Pack Loader jar, BetterModel (managed plugin), node-2 Test Flight, sound render path, Blender, catalog index.
6. **Switch features on**, preview accounts first, one line at a time (designer, item states, data pack then worldgen, creatures, studios settings, import, Test Flight gate then block-on-fail, managed plugins then delivery, Mod Packs, sound library cleared, catalog tools, pass-rate page ...): see the table in the runbook; rollback = set the flag back and restart the same process.
7. **Public launch**: the pair `cyrus_studio_public_enabled` + `cyrus_tok_live` together, last (`FLIP=yes bash scripts/cyrus/deploy-modbuilder.sh` refuses unless `auth=api_key`). Rollback: set both false (settings are read on every request, immediate).
8. **Verification jobs** (no deploy needed): eval run, real-client test day.
Read-only smoke: `scripts/cyrus/smoke-readonly.sh [all|migrations|service|worker|flags|packs|delivery]` (no writes, no restarts, no model calls, never prints a secret; exits 1 on FAIL).

## Flags, settings and env
Full generated registry: [reference/flags-and-env.md](reference/flags-and-env.md) (about 320 names with default, where read, meaning). Structure: **env flags** `CYRUS_*` (web/worker/scripts; changing one needs an env edit + restart), **service env** `MB_*` (build service run.sh), **Settings** `cyrus_*` (DB, admin Flags tab, read every request, instant), plus the admin settings catalog (`lib/cyrus/admin/settings-catalog.ts`). Kill switches (instant, fail closed): `cyrus_builds_paused` (global build pause), AI gateway kill, `cyrus_mod_networking_enabled`, the launch pair. Helper to flip a setting by hand: `/root/agent-notes/set-setting.sh <key> <value>` (owner).

## Build lock, memory and load
One heavy job at a time on node-2 (builds, `devhost test|build|run --lock`). Many agents queue; weekly model usage is the other limit. node-2's agent slice has OOM-killed `next dev` (5+ GB) several times: run screenshots in batches and restart. Always `devhost stop all` and `devhost rm` when finished. Fixtures that import `lib/auth` need `scripts/cyrus/server-only-shim.cjs`.

## Observability and backups (r37, built, NOT installed)
`GET /api/cyrus/health` (names the release commit via `CYRUS_RELEASE_COMMIT`), error hook (`CYRUS_ERROR_WEBHOOK_URL`, scrubbed, deduplicated Discord), cost export (`scripts/cyrus/cost-export.sh`), alert rules and checker (`scripts/cyrus/alert-check.sh`, `deploy/cyrus/cyrus-alerts.service`, spend alert `CYRUS_SPEND_ALERT_USD`), uptime list and status-page spec, nightly **encrypted** backup (`scripts/cyrus/backup-nightly.sh`, public-key encryption, remote target, library files opt-in, SFX only encrypted; keys not in the repo). Cyrus has no backups of its own tables beyond Nxeon's Postgres backups until the data split; the proprietary SFX library has a single copy.

## Cloudflare for the Nxeon zones (groundwork only)
`deploy/cloudflare/` + `scripts/cloudflare/`: real client IP restored from `CF-Connecting-IP` only from Cloudflare ranges (generated nginx config, weekly updater, throwaway-nginx simulation 6/6), three first-hop X-Forwarded-For call sites fixed, static-only cache rules, websocket keepalive, origin certs. Keep game, mail, SSH and panel records grey (DNS only); keep `NXEON_TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS=1`. **Blocker**: Nxeon's terminal and console WebSocket servers send no pings, so Cloudflare would drop idle sessions after about 100 s. Nothing here is applied.

## Incident playbooks (past outages and how not to repeat them)
| Incident | Cause | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Two prod outages 2026-10-01 | raw `npm run build` + restart in the live tree | Deploy only via deploy-staging -> promote-production; builds run on node-2. |
| Primary hard crash 2026-10-06 | parallel agent builds (load 16+, swap full) | All heavy work on node-2 via `devhost`; cap agent builds. |
| Prod DB ownership moved cluster-wide 2026-10-07 | an agent ran `REASSIGN OWNED` | Forbid role/ownership SQL in every agent brief; never give agents prod DB credentials. |
| Root disk full 2026-09-27 (Postgres crashed, prod 500 for about 10 min) | build caches on `/` | Never write to the primary root disk; clear only known-safe caches. |
| `pkill -f "next start"` restarted live prod | pattern kill | Kill by port PID or systemd unit only. |
| `git add -A` in a symlinked worktree could replace prod's node_modules with a self-referential symlink | worktree + symlink | Never `git add -A`; never symlink node_modules; add paths by name. |
| Rollback-incomplete on a revoke mid-update (r38 run) | rollback re-creating an existing parent folder was refused | Fixed; delivery now reports `rollback_incomplete` honestly and restores exact bytes. |
| Stuck at "Compiling" in the prod studio (2026-10) | root cause not found; service answered in 0.4 s, nginx fine | Stream-silence watchdog (30 s, re-attach) in `lib/cyrus/forge.ts`. |
| rc1 type check out of memory (found 2026-10-11, never deployed) | the merged Cyrus tree had never been through `next build`; one structural PrismaClient comparison in `lib/cyrus/host/nxeon.ts` cost ~1.1M types per program, and the whole program needs ~6.3 GB heap (main: 3.5 GB) against Node's 4 GB default in the promote | Fixed on `release/cyrus-rc1`: cast through `unknown`, `next build` checks the app via `tsconfig.next.json`, `npm run build` sets a 6 GB heap. Run full `tsc` with `devhost run -- env NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=7168 npx tsc --noEmit` (`devhost tsc`'s 5 GB preset now dies silently). |
| A promote that rolled itself back | overloaded primary failed the health check | Quiet hour, no agent builds, retry. |
| Build host VMs could not reach nxeon.cloud (hairpin firewall) | firewall rule, fixed 2026-08-23 | See the Nxeon firewall notes; check this first if flights cannot fetch from the site. |

If a Cyrus build fails for a customer: check `/admin/cyrus/builds/<id>` (engine release record, flight verdict, errors), then the service `/health`; our-side failures are free for the customer (token release). If node-2 is down say so; do not fall back to building on the primary.

#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# devhost — run agent dev work on the BUILD HOST (node-2), not on the primary.
#
# Edit files on the primary as usual (your own git worktree — never /opt/nxeon),
# then run every heavy command through this helper. It mirrors your worktree's
# source to node-2 (/tank/nxeon-build/wt/<name>, own node_modules there), runs the
# command inside the capped nxeon-build-agents.slice with a THROWAWAY database
# (Postgres on node-2 127.0.0.1:5433), and streams the output back.
#
#   scripts/devhost run [--lock] [--max SEC] -- CMD...   push + run CMD in the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost tsc                                  = run -- npx tsc --noEmit
#   scripts/devhost test [FILES...]                      = run --lock -- npx tsx --test ...
#   scripts/devhost build                                = run --lock -- npx next build
#   scripts/devhost dev [--port P]                       start `next dev` on node-2 (background unit)
#   scripts/devhost bg NAME [--port P] -- CMD...         any background process (worker, preview server)
#   scripts/devhost stop [NAME|all]                      stop this worktree's background units
#   scripts/devhost logs [NAME] [-n N] [-f]              journal of a background unit (default: dev)
#   scripts/devhost tunnel PORT [LOCAL_PORT]             ssh -L so the primary can curl/Playwright it
#   scripts/devhost pull REMOTE_PATH [LOCAL_DEST]        copy results (screenshots, reports) back
#   scripts/devhost push                                 just sync files (run does this itself)
#   scripts/devhost install                              force npm install + prisma generate there
#   scripts/devhost db push|reset|info                   throwaway DB: schema push / recreate / name
#   scripts/devhost env set KEY=VALUE | unset KEY | list extra env for this worktree (never prod secrets)
#   scripts/devhost rm                                   stop units, drop the throwaway DB, delete the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost ls | status | sync                   workspaces / node-2 load / push refs to node-2's mirror
#
# Rules: /root/agent-notes/BUILD-HOST.md. The node-2 copy is a build/run sandbox,
# not a place to edit or commit — your primary-side worktree stays the source of truth.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
HERE="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")"
# shellcheck source=lib/buildhost-env.sh
source "$HERE/lib/buildhost-env.sh"
REPO="${DEVHOST_REPO:-/opt/nxeon}"

die() { echo "devhost: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
say() { echo "devhost: $*" >&2; }
q() { printf '%q ' "$@"; }

# ---- workspace identity -----------------------------------------------------
worktree_root() {
  local top; top=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || die "run this inside your own git worktree of the Nxeon repo"
  top=$(readlink -f "$top")
  case "$top" in
    /opt/nxeon|/opt/nxeon-staging|/tank/nxeon-deploy/*) die "$top is a live/deploy tree. Create your own worktree first:  git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/dev-worktrees/<name> -b <branch> main" ;;
  esac
  [ -L "$top/.next" ] && die "$top/.next is a symlink (a live tree) — refusing"
  [ -L "$top/node_modules" ] && say "warning: $top/node_modules is a symlink — never 'git add -A' here (see BUILD-HOST.md). devhost does not need local node_modules at all."
  echo "$top"
}
ws_name() {
  local top="$1" n
  n=$(basename "$top" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z' | tr -c 'a-z0-9-\n' '-' | sed -E 's/-+/-/g; s/^-//; s/-$//' | cut -c1-40)
  [ -n "$n" ] || n=wt
  echo "${DEVHOST_NAME:-$n}"
}
init_ws() {
  TOP=$(worktree_root); NAME=$(ws_name "$TOP")
  case "$NAME" in *[!a-z0-9-]*|"") die "bad workspace name '$NAME' (DEVHOST_NAME=...)";; esac

model CyrusPersonalApiKey {
  id         String    @id @default(cuid())
  userId     String
  name       String
  /// the 8 characters after "cyk_", shown in the list so the owner can recognise a key
  prefix     String
  sha256     String    @unique
  scopes     String[]
  createdAt  DateTime  @default(now())
  lastUsedAt DateTime?
  expiresAt  DateTime?
  revokedAt  DateTime?

  @@index([userId, createdAt])
}

/// A customer's Cyrus data export or deletion request (handled by staff; see docs "Cyrus customer app").
model CyrusDataRequest {
  id          String    @id @default(cuid())
  userId      String
  /// export | delete
  kind        String
  /// requested | in_progress | ready | expired | done | failed | cancelled (r44 jobs: lib/cyrus/app/data-jobs.ts)
  status        String    @default("requested")
  note          String?
  createdAt     DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedAt     DateTime  @updatedAt
  completedAt   DateTime?
  /// r44: a deletion runs after this (cancellable until then)
  graceUntil    DateTime?
  startedAt     DateTime?
  attempts      Int       @default(0)
  error         String?
  /// r44 export: the archive on disk (CYRUS_DATA_EXPORT_DIR), downloadable by the owner until expiresAt
  archivePath   String?
  archiveBytes  Int?
  archiveSha256 String?
  expiresAt     DateTime?
  /// r44: per-table counts of what was exported / deleted / anonymised / retained
  result        Json?

  @@index([userId, kind, status])
  @@index([kind, status, createdAt])
}

content.thinking:
I'm sketching a realistic commit plan: starting with a pure, client-safe pricing module that defines default storage quota settings for different tiers, plus accompanying tests.

I'm also working out the tiered pricing table and various configuration constants—grace periods, disk cost per GB, alert thresholds, and an enforcement flag. I'm weighing whether enforcement should be gated by an environment flag like `CYRUS_STORAGE` so the feature stays off by default and follows the codebase's existing convention for rollout flags, while still being fail-closed once enabled.

For the actual cost calculation, I'm defining the cost of n GB as the cheaper of either paying the literal rate for n, or buying up to a higher breakpoint tier outright—since sometimes a bigger tier is actually cheaper than the exact amount needed. Working through the numbers, this means several usage levels in the 1-49 GB range all end up costing the same $15, since it's cheaper to just buy the 50GB tier outright than pay the literal per-GB rate at that size.

So the "never higher for fewer GB" monotonic property holds across tiers, which I'll verify with test cases showing the cost table. I'm also thinking through storing prices in cents as integers to avoid rounding issues, and setting up config validation rules like ascending minGb thresholds, bounded cent values, and a max tier count, plus working out proration logic for plan changes.

For upgrades, I'll charge the prorated difference immediately; for downgrades or cancellations, the change takes effect at the next renewal with no mid-period refund, and quota stays until period end. The trickier part is interpreting what happens when someone goes over quota after downgrading — whether there's a 30-day grace period where builds/uploads still work, or if it immediately goes read-only.

I'll settle on: over-quota triggered by a downgrade, cancellation, or expiry gets a 30-day grace window where writes still work (with a warning banner), and only after grace expires does it become read-only for new builds, uploads, and contributions. But if someone goes over quota through their own normal usage in real time, that blocks immediately with no grace period, since data is never deleted automatically either way.

For enforcement specifics: builds block once usage hits full quota (since byte size isn't known in advance), uploads block if the new size would push past quota, and library contributions block when storage is full. A refunded add-on purchase cancels immediately, drops the quota, and starts the grace period rather than deleting anything.

For the accounting module, I'm designing content-addressed tracking where each item (builds/jars/source, assets, packs, drafts, uploads, library contributions) is keyed by sha256 and byte size, deduped per account, with items lacking a hash (like drafts or uploads) getting a synthetic path-based key instead. I'm sketching a pure usage-computation function that takes these items and returns totals broken down by category.

I'm now tracing the actual server-side data sources that feed this: ModBuild rows carry jarSha256/jarSize plus Cyrus metadata linking to project and game, CyrusProjectAsset rows link assets back to owning users through their project, and revisions store manifest entries with sha256 but no explicit size, so I need to figure out where the actual file bytes live for those. I'm also noting that shared blobs used across multiple mods should be counted once in the account total but shown per-mod in each mod's individual view.

Since manifest entries lack sizes, I'll fall back to estimating revision storage from the spec and manifest JSON row size itself, keyed under a `rev:<id>` category. Beyond revisions, I need to account for packs (via FsModPackStore's version list with sha256/bytes), drafts (JSON doc length keyed by `draft:<id>`), raw uploads sitting in the uploads directory plus any build attachments, and library contributions tied to users through CyrusCatalogEntry -- I still need to confirm whether that entry stores an explicit byte size field. For persisting all this, I'm planning a new CyrusStorageUsage table keyed by userId with usedBytes, a JSON breakdown, a computedAt timestamp, and a version, populated by a recompute job with support for incremental updates.

For incremental updates, rather than tracking per-sha dedupe state, I'll mark accounts dirty after writes and let a sweep recompute just the dirty ones cheaply, while also bumping a `pendingBytes` field on the usage row immediately so quota enforcement stays responsive between sweeps -- pendingBytes clears once the full recompute runs. I also want a CyrusStorageAddon table for purchased extra storage (gb, pendingGb for scheduled downgrades, status, billing period fields, cancelAtPeriodEnd, idempotency key, charge reference), plus a `graceUntil` field on the usage row for soft quota overages, and a separate CyrusStorageCharge ledger table for idempotent purchase records.

Simplifying down to two tables: a combined CyrusStorageAccount holding both usage and addon state per user (usedBytes, pendingBytes, addon tier/status/period info, grace/over-quota timestamps), and CyrusStorageCharge for idempotent money events (kind, gb range, cents, method, reference, refunds). I'm using BigInt for byte counts since gigabyte-scale values exceed Int32, converting to Number() where needed for JSON serialization.

I still need functions for quota bytes, prorating upgrades/downgrades mid-period (charging the price difference scaled by remaining time, deferring downgrades to period end), and a meter level classifier for usage warnings at 80%/95%/full. I'm also deciding whether to define GB as 1024^3 bytes (GiB) or the decimal standard most providers show customers -- leaning toward using GiB under the "GB" label since that's common practice.

I'm now working through the state machine for write decisions under storage quotas: it should allow writes when enforcement is disabled, synchronously compute a missing usage row rather than failing closed on unknown usage (since that would block brand-new users), and otherwise sum used, pending, and incoming bytes against the quota to decide.

For the over-quota case, I'm figuring out a grace-period rule — when a recompute first detects usage exceeding quota, I set a grace deadline rather than refusing immediately, since gate checks already prevent most self-inflicted overages except builds whose size isn't known upfront. The tricky part is distinguishing an overage caused by the user's own writes versus one caused by a quota drop (downgrade, cancellation, refund, plan lapse), so I'm leaning toward a uniform rule that triggers grace whenever the recompute first observes usage exceeding quota, regardless of cause.

For builds, I'll keep the gate simple: require total usage strictly below quota rather than tracking a reserve estimate, so full just means used ≥ quota. Now I'm defining a pure accounting module with storage category types covering builds, assets, revisions, packs, drafts, and uploads.

Still writing types and rollup logic... Keys are content-addressed via sha256 hash when possible, otherwise fall back to a table/id reference. Now I'm starting the server-side collector function that gathers account items per user, beginning with mod build jar hashes and sizes.

I need to verify how attachment sizes and CyrusMeta shapes are structured, and check whether build sources are also stored as zips somewhere. Then I'm tracing through projects, project assets, and revisions tied to a user, figuring out how to attribute byte sizes and mod/game associations for each.

For revisions I'm sizing spec, manifest, and engine data per row using raw SQL with `pg_column_size`, since computing that in JS would be too heavy for thousands of rows -- I'll inject this through a sources interface so tests can use fakes while the real implementation hits the database directly. Now I'm extending the same approach to drafts, sizing the document column by owner reference.

For packs I'm pulling from the FsModPackStore, listing versions keyed by sha256 with byte counts at the pack level. Uploads get tallied by reading the user's upload directory and stat-ing pending files with a 24-hour TTL. For library contributions I'm querying the catalog entries scoped to the contributor, excluding removed status, and only when the library secret is configured -- with a dedupe rule so an asset that's both a project asset and a library contribution under the same hash only counts once.

Finally I'm sketching the `recompute` flow for the storage account: gather all these sources, roll them up, compute the quota from tier plus addons, detect if the quota just dropped (triggering a grace period), then persist the usage totals and breakdown as JSON.

I need to add incremental tracking too -- a `noteWrite` call that atomically bumps pending bytes and flags the row dirty, plus a sweep job that recomputes dirty or stale rows in batches and takes daily snapshots, hooked into the existing worker schedule behind a feature flag. I'll need to wire `noteWrite` into the various write paths -- upload saves, generic asset recording, mod jar storage, and pack saves -- as a best-effort, flag-gated call. And I'm planning a server-side `checkStorageWrite` gate that short-circuits to allow when the feature is disabled.

For enforcement, I'm deciding where to call the gate: both mod build creation paths should return a 507 "storage_full" error when the user is over quota, the upload route should gate on the upload size, and I'm considering whether the import route needs gating too. The tricky question is whether to put the check inside `recordAsset` itself (which would couple the pure engine-core store to the storage system) or instead gate at the studio API routes that call it -- leaning toward the latter despite more routes needing changes.

The purchase flow checks a feature flag plus wallet availability, validates the gb amount against a max, and computes a prorated price if an addon is already active, then charges the wallet and delivers the storage change, with a refund compensation path on failure. I'm also designing `applyStorageEvent` to be idempotent via a unique key, creating charge records and updating the account's addon status and billing period on completion, and handling refund reversals when a charge is refunded.

content.thinking:
I'm organizing the second commit around accounting and enforcement—schema tables, the collector, recompute logic, sweep job, gating, hooks, and backend cleanup—while leaving the add-on purchase backend for the commit with its UI. Now I'm defining the Prisma model for per-account storage tracking.

Still defining the schema...

I'm adding a daily storage snapshot model to track totals and account breakdowns, then wiring the new tables into CyrusDb's type picks and starting a pure accounting module to define storage categories like builds, assets, and revisions.

I'm sketching types for storage items and per-mod rollups, with each item carrying a category, byte count, and ownership metadata so I can attribute shared blobs and aggregate totals by mod and category later.

Mod sums can exceed the total when files are shared, so I'll document that shared files count once overall but appear per-mod. Items without a mod (packs, pending uploads, library) fall outside byMod but still count in byCategory, with games defaulting to "minecraft" or "unassigned" when unknown. I'm defining a StorageSources interface to fetch builds and projects per user for testable collection.

Still writing interface methods...

I'm deriving mod IDs: builds use rootBuildId or id with pluginName as label, projects use rootBuildId or a prefixed project id, and build attachments are tracked as uploads keyed by build and index. Library entries use their sha256 as the identifying key.

I need to dedupe entries that appear across categories (like a library item matching a project asset by sha), prioritizing attribution in order: builds, assets, packs, revisions, drafts, uploads, library. Pack zip bytes count as distinct content from their member jars, so they're sized fully on their own.

Now I'm writing the raw SQL for prismaSources, starting with a query against CyrusRevision that sums the sizes of spec, manifest, and engine columns per revision to compute byte totals.

Writing size queries...

Builds should only count jar bytes if jarPath is non-null and jarSize exists, so cleanup operations that null out jarPath automatically exclude removed jars from the tally.

Still writing recomputeStorage...

I'm also noting a potential race where pendingBytes incremented between collecting items and writing the row could be lost, though this is acceptable since the recompute would include those bytes if the write happened before the collection step.

For the over-state logic, I'm defining a pure function that decides grace periods: if usage is under quota, clear overSince and graceUntil; if over quota, set overSince once and only grant a grace window when the quota itself dropped below prior usage, otherwise mark it read-only immediately without grace.

For launch fairness, I'm also deciding that a brand-new row with no prior recompute (first-ever measurement over quota) should also get a grace period, not just quota drops -- otherwise existing users already over 1GB would be instantly locked out when the feature ships. Now moving to gating the actual write check function by user ID.

The function first short-circuits if storage isn't enabled, then looks up or recomputes a stale account row (older than 24h triggers recompute), and feeds the usage/quota/add numbers into the decision helper, failing closed with a "storage_unknown" refusal if anything throws. I'm also noting that the quota stored on the row could go stale between plan or add-on changes and the next recompute, so instead of trusting the cached quotaBytes, I should cheaply recompute the tier and add-on based quota right at gate time.

The decision helper itself is pure logic: it sums used plus pending bytes, checks whether adding the new bytes keeps the total under quota, and only allows a write that would exceed quota if there's an active grace period. Beyond that, I'm sketching a message generator for the full-storage error and a noteWrite function that increments pendingBytes for a user as writes happen.

For the sweep job, I'm planning markDirty for individual users plus a periodic storageSweep that recomputes stale or dirty rows, handles add-on renewals, and builds a daily usage snapshot if one doesn't exist yet, scheduled every five minutes. Then I need to wire the storage gate into the create.ts handlers and the uploads route so they return a 507 with a storage_full code when the check fails, checking that the fail() helper can accept arbitrary status codes.

For engine-core's recordAsset, I'm figuring out how to gate non-generated asset creation and call noteWrite afterward, which requires resolving the userId from the project via a database lookup, and I'm weighing whether to add a dedupe check using a raw SQL join between project assets and projects filtered by userId and sha256, though I'm unsure how that interacts with the test suite's fake vs real database setup.

I need to throw EngineStoreError with code "storage_full" when the gate refuses, but I should check how studios' http layer maps that error code to a status (400 vs 507 vs 500), so I'll grep for e.code handling in studios/http.ts. Beyond recordAsset, I still need to wire the same storage gate into library contributions, mod pack version saves, import routes, and the jar landing path in modbuilder's store sync.

Now I'm designing the cleanup backend: a cleanupCandidates function that identifies old build jars safe to remove — excluding the newest build in each chain, anything still referenced by a pack or an installed/lastInstall version — flagging builds past the retention window as "suggested" removals and everything else eligible as "can remove," plus similar retention logic for stale drafts and uploads.

For deletion, I'm requiring an exact "DELETE" confirmation phrase, rechecking ownership and eligibility per id, then only unlinking jar files confined to the MODBUILD_DIR path before nulling out the jarPath in the database (while preserving jarSha256/jarSize for history) and recording a storageCleanup timestamp/size in the ModBuild's metadata. I'm accepting that if a jar is later requested after removal, the read will fail gracefully with a message explaining it was cleared to save space and would need a rebuild.

I'll also add deleteDrafts and audit logging for each cleanup action, keeping scope limited to build jars, drafts, and uploads given time constraints. Next I want to check the fail() helper in create.ts, the studios HTTP error mapping, the modpack save path, and the import route gating logic.

For refunds, I'm tracking cumulative refunded amounts against the original charge and only taking action once the refund is complete and tied to the currently active charge.

I'm defining a helper to determine if a given charge is the "in-force" one by comparing its period end and gigabyte amount to the account's current state, then writing a buyStorage function for wallet purchases that validates the add-on is enabled, checks gigabyte limits, and computes a plan change -- scheduling decreases for later, no-oping on same values, and handling increases/new purchases by calculating the charge amount, with a special case for zero-cost adjustments.

For non-zero charges, I'm locking on a wallet reference, checking for an existing idempotent charge, deducting from the wallet, then delivering the storage change either as a pending purchase event or applying it directly, with compensating refunds on failure. I'm also sketching out cancelStorage and resume logic that toggle the next-period gigabyte target, and starting to think through the renewal sweep that processes active add-on accounts.

For the renewal sweep itself, each account either drops to zero and gets canceled, or gets charged a renewal fee keyed by the period end timestamp, advancing the period by a month (guarding against drifting too far behind if the sweep is delayed). If funds are insufficient, I'm flagging the account past_due so the effective quota calculation treats it as inactive and the storage allotment drops accordingly.

For retry logic, past_due accounts should get picked up by the sweep again, retried at most once per day, with full cancellation after about a week of nonpayment. Card-based add-ons are different — Stripe handles renewal itself, so I just skip those in the sweep and rely on the invoice.paid webhook to apply the renewal.

I decide to work around it by creating a fresh price object on the fly via `prices.create` and then updating the subscription item to point to that new price, which handles both increases and decreases. I'm scoping the card add-on logic to a handler covering invoice.paid for purchases/renewals, subscription deleted for lapses, and charge.refunded for reversals (tracing the charge back through its invoice to the subscription), plus cancel_at_period_end for downgrades.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /tmp/claude-0/bundled-skills/2.1.289/0116a2a6aaa25ff5fd31e2b67a3dc913/dataviz

# Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values - touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe - run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.

## The procedure - do these in order

Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.

1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job - magnitude, identity, polarity, a
   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). -> `references/choosing-a-form.md`
2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) - each has one rule.
   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. -> `references/color-formula.md`
3. **VALIDATE the palette - run the script, don't reason about Delta E.**
   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,...>" --mode light` (relative to
   this skill's base directory - or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
   chart's own page, where it reads
   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
   the baseline, 2px lines, >=8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
   selective direct labels. -> `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
5. **Add the hover layer - by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. -> `references/interaction.md`
6. **Final accessibility pass.** For >= 2 series a legend is always present and <= 4
   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box - the title names
   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** - its own
   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout - open or
   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
   before calling it done.

Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** - it is the catalog
of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.

## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)

- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
  generated hue - it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
  scale -> two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
  #1 chart mistake - see anti-patterns.)*
- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
  count must not repaint the survivors.
- **Sequential = one hue, light->dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD Delta E >= 8 is the
  target (OKLab ×100); 6-8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A
  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL - full-color readers can't tell the
  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse
  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead - see check 4. A contrast WARN
  obligates visible labels or a table view - it is not dismissable.
- **Thin marks; a legend always present for >= 2 series (none for one), with
  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** - values, labels, and legends
  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.

## Plugging in a design system

The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
instance - every value filled in - is `references/palette.md`.

| Parameter | What the system provides |
|---|---|
| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical - steps distinct from categorical |
| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |

To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

## Reference files

| File | What it answers |
|------|-----------------|
| `references/choosing-a-form.md` | Which chart type / is it even a chart? |
| `references/color-formula.md` | The four jobs, the six checks, snap-to-passing |
| `references/marks-and-anatomy.md` | Mark specs, spacers, labels, figures, hero number |
| `references/interaction.md` | Tooltips & hover, filters & time ranges |
| `references/components.md` | The pieces a chart is made of - build each in plain HTML |
| `references/anti-patterns.md` | **What goes wrong - check every chart against this** |
| `references/palette.md` | **The reference palette instance** - every parameter, filled in; swap for your brand's |
| `scripts/validate_palette.js` | Runnable six-checks validator (run it; don't eyeball) |

#!/bin/bash
# Cyrus storage report (r51): disk/pool usage on the primary and node-2 plus the sizes of the directories Cyrus (and its
# backups) use, as ONE JSON file the admin Storage tab reads (CYRUS_STORAGE_REPORT, default /var/lib/cyrus/storage-report.json).
# READ ONLY: df, du and `zpool list` only; never deletes or moves anything. du over /tank/backup takes minutes: run it
# nightly (deploy/cyrus/cyrus-storage-report.timer, NOT INSTALLED), never in a request.
#   scripts/cyrus/storage-report.sh [--dry-run]          (--dry-run prints the JSON instead of writing it)
# Env: CYRUS_STORAGE_REPORT, BUILD_HOST (node-2 over ssh; empty = skip node-2), CYRUS_STORAGE_REPORT_DIRS (extra
# "label=path" pairs, comma separated, on the primary).
set -euo pipefail
OUT="${CYRUS_STORAGE_REPORT:-/var/lib/cyrus/storage-report.json}"
NODE2="${BUILD_HOST-root@178.63.94.114}"
DRY=0; [ "${1:-}" = "--dry-run" ] && DRY=1
SSH_OPTS=(-o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=15)
# label=path on the primary (missing paths are reported as missing, not errors)
PRIMARY_DIRS="modbuilds=${NXEON_MODBUILD_DIR:-/var/lib/nxeon/modbuilds},packs=${CYRUS_PACK_LOCAL_DIR:-/tank/cyrus-packs},library-store=${CYRUS_LIBRARY_LOCAL_DIR:-/tank/cyrus-library-store},library-staging=${CYRUS_LIBRARY_STAGING_DIR:-/tank/cyrus-library-staging},exports=${CYRUS_DATA_EXPORT_DIR:-/var/lib/nxeon/cyrus-exports},imports=${CYRUS_IMPORT_DIR:-/var/lib/nxeon/cyrus-imports},backups=/tank/backup,nxlabs-mirror=/tank/nxlabs-mirror${CYRUS_STORAGE_REPORT_DIRS:+,$CYRUS_STORAGE_REPORT_DIRS}"
NODE2_DIRS="sound-library=/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/sound-library/files,motion-effects=/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/motion,cyrus-backups=/tank/cyrus-backups,dev-worktrees=/tank/nxeon-build/wt"

collect() { # $1 = dirs list; prints NDJSON lines (runs locally or remotely)
  df -P -B1 / /tank 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR>1 {printf "{\"t\":\"disk\",\"mount\":\"%s\",\"size\":%s,\"used\":%s,\"avail\":%s}\n", $6, $2, $3, $4}' | sort -u
  if command -v zpool >/dev/null 2>&1; then zpool list -Hp -o name,size,alloc,free 2>/dev/null | awk '{printf "{\"t\":\"pool\",\"mount\":\"zpool:%s\",\"size\":%s,\"used\":%s,\"avail\":%s}\n", $1, $2, $3, $4}'; fi
  IFS=',' read -ra PAIRS <<< "$1"
  for p in "${PAIRS[@]}"; do
    l="${p%%=*}"; d="${p#*=}"
    if [ -d "$d" ]; then b=$(timeout 1800 du -sb --apparent-size "$d" 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}'); echo "{\"t\":\"dir\",\"label\":\"$l\",\"path\":\"$d\",\"bytes\":${b:-0}}"; else echo "{\"t\":\"dir\",\"label\":\"$l\",\"path\":\"$d\",\"missing\":true}"; fi
  done
}
PRIMARY=$(collect "$PRIMARY_DIRS" | sed 's/^{/{"host":"primary",/')
REMOTE=""
if [ -n "$NODE2" ]; then
  REMOTE=$(ssh "${SSH_OPTS[@]}" "$NODE2" "$(declare -f collect); collect '$NODE2_DIRS'" 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^{/{"host":"node-2",/' || echo '{"host":"node-2","t":"error","error":"unreachable"}')
fi
JSON=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$PRIMARY" "$REMOTE" | grep -v '^$' | node -e 'const l=require("fs").readFileSync(0,"utf8").trim().split("\n").map((x)=>JSON.parse(x));process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({schema:1,at:new Date().toISOString(),rows:l},null,1))')
if [ "$DRY" = 1 ]; then echo "$JSON"; exit 0; fi
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"; printf '%s\n' "$JSON" > "$OUT.tmp" && mv "$OUT.tmp" "$OUT"
echo "storage report written: $OUT"
EOF

# "label=path" pairs, comma separated, on the primary).
set -euo pipefail
OUT="${CYRUS_STORAGE_REPORT:-/var/lib/cyrus/storage-report.json}"
NODE2="${BUILD_HOST-root@178.63.94.114}"
DRY=0; [ "${1:-}" = "--dry-run" ] && DRY=1
SSH_OPTS=(-o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=15)
# label=path on the primary (missing paths are reported as missing, not errors)
PRIMARY_DIRS="modbuilds=${NXEON_MODBUILD_DIR:-/var/lib/nxeon/modbuilds},packs=${CYRUS_PACK_LOCAL_DIR:-/tank/cyrus-packs},library-store=${CYRUS_LIBRARY_LOCAL_DIR:-/tank/cyrus-library-store},library-staging=${CYRUS_LIBRARY_STAGING_DIR:-/tank/cyrus-library-staging},exports=${CYRUS_DATA_EXPORT_DIR:-/var/lib/nxeon/cyrus-exports},imports=${CYRUS_IMPORT_DIR:-/var/lib/nxeon/cyrus-imports},backups=/tank/backup,nxlabs-mirror=/tank/nxlabs-mirror${CYRUS_STORAGE_REPORT_DIRS:+,$CYRUS_STORAGE_REPORT_DIRS}"

collect() { # $1 = dirs list; prints NDJSON lines (runs locally or remotely)
  df -P -B1 / /tank 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR>1 {printf "{\"t\":\"disk\",\"mount\":\"%s\",\"size\":%s,\"used\":%s,\"avail\":%s}\n", $6, $2, $3, $4}' | sort -u

Extra storage is a monthly Nxeon product (`cyrus.storage.addon`), switch `CYRUS_STORAGE_ADDONS` (needs `CYRUS_STORAGE`), code `lib/cyrus/storage/addon.ts`. **Price**: the owner's per-GB bands (1 GB $0.85, 5 GB $0.75, 25 GB $0.60, 50 GB $0.30, 100 GB $0.20) in setting `cyrus_storage_price_table`; rule `cyrus_storage_pricing_rule` = `capped` (default, an ASSUMPTION pending the owner: cost(n) = min(rate(n) x n, min over higher breakpoints b of rate(b) x b), so fewer GB never cost more; 20-50 GB all cost $15.00, 67-100 GB $20.00), `literal` (the cliff: 49 GB $29.40 > 50 GB $15.00) or `graduated`. Placeholders until confirmed (OWNER-ACTIONS "r51").
- **Wallet** (default): reference `cst:<user>:g<gb>:<key>` is the wallet reference AND the idemKey (`CyrusStorageCharge.idemKey` UNIQUE), so the direct apply, the signed purchase webhook (envelope `kind: "storage"`, same receiver `/api/cyrus/purchase-events`), a redelivery, the wallet reconcile (`reconcileStorageCharges`) and the entitlement mirror apply a charge once. A failed apply after the charge refunds the wallet (compensating `:refund`).
- **Changes**: increase = the price difference for the rest of the period, charged now (rounded up); decrease or cancel = at the period end (never a mid-period refund). **Renewal**: the storage sweep charges the wallet once per period (`renew_<periodEnd ms>` key), retries a failed renewal daily for 7 days (status `past_due`, quota back to the plan's), then cancels. **Refund** of the charge in force takes its GB back. A quota drop starts a 30-day grace; nothing is deleted.
- **Card**: a Stripe subscription on Nxeon's account with an inline monthly price (`openStorageCheckout`, embedded checkout, return `/api/cyrus/storage/return`); `invoice.paid` / `customer.subscription.*` / `charge.refunded` for storage subscriptions are handled BEFORE the plan handler so a storage subscription is never mirrored as a plan. Built, **not run against Stripe**; GB changes on a card add-on = cancel and buy again.
- **Entitlement sync**: Nxeon's snapshot carries an optional `storage` array (wallet `cst:` charges with refunds; absent when empty, so older receivers see the same shape); the Cyrus mirror applies any it has not (`applyMirroredStorageCharge`) and refuses another account's reference.
- Tests: `test/cyrus-storage-db.test.ts` (8, throwaway Postgres: buy once on retry, prorated increase, decrease at renewal, renewal once, cancel -> lapse + grace, refund reverses once, insufficient funds, event/mirror/reconcile once), `test/cyrus-storage-addon.test.ts`, `test/cyrus-storage-pricing.test.ts` (prints the price table).

''')
ins('docs/cyrus/06-portals.md','## The v5/v6 studio','''## Storage (r51)
Switch `CYRUS_STORAGE` (off = nothing measured or blocked). Code `lib/cyrus/storage/*`, tables `CyrusStorageAccount`, `CyrusStorageCharge`, `CyrusStorageSnapshot` (SQL `prisma/manual-migrations/2026-10-11-cyrus-storage.sql`, not applied).
- **Quotas** (settings, placeholders): Free `cyrus_storage_quota_free_gb` 1 GB (the owner set none), Katara 5, Saka 25, Yakko (`all`) 50 GB, plus the add-on ([05](05-bridge-and-accounts.md#storage-add-on-r51)). 1 GB = 2^30 bytes.
- **What counts** (`accounting.ts`): build jars, the build's hosted resource pack and data packs, project assets, revisions (spec + manifest + engine column sizes), Mod Pack versions, studio drafts, uploads and build attachments, library contributions the account owns (opaque contributor id). Content-addressed bytes count ONCE per account (first category wins); per mod and per game a shared file shows in each. Not counted: the shared library itself, other creators' content, installs on servers.
- **Where it is measured** (`collect.ts` + `collect-db.ts`): ModBuild rows (`NXEON_MODBUILD_DIR`), `CyrusProjectAsset`, `CyrusRevision`, `CyrusModelDraft`, the modpacks store, the uploads directory, `CyrusCatalogEntry`. Full recompute per account (on first use, when stale after 24 h, on a quota drop, by the sweep for dirty rows); incremental `pendingBytes` on every write.
- **Enforcement** (`service.ts checkStorageWrite`, server side, FAILS CLOSED: 503 `storage_unknown` if usage cannot be read, 507 `storage_full` when full): both build create paths, uploads, engine-core `recordAsset` (customer-added bytes; the same sha256 already in the account adds nothing), the studio auto-contribution (skipped, the save still works), API v1 contribute, new Mod Pack versions, imports. Installing, keeping, downloading and exporting are never gated (pinned by a test).
- **Over quota**: a quota drop (downgrade, cancel, refund, failed renewal, plan lapse) or the first measurement over quota starts a 30-day grace (`cyrus_storage_grace_days`) where writes still work; after it new writes are refused until under quota. Going over by your own writes has no grace. Data is NEVER deleted automatically.
- **Customer UI**: Account > Storage (`components/cyrus/app/StorageView.tsx`): meter with 80/95/100% levels (`cyrus_storage_warn_pcts`), "storage full" state with Add storage / Free up space, breakdown per category, per game, per mod; the buy-more **slider** (`StoragePanels.tsx`) priced by the same function the server charges, a same-price hint, the prorated upgrade line and a price chart (your price vs the literal rate); **cleanup** of old build jars (never the newest version, an installed one, a pack member or a project head; history kept), drafts and pending uploads, with a typed DELETE confirm, audited. Retention suggestions after `cyrus_storage_retention_days`.

## Admin storage (r51)
`/admin/cyrus/storage` (tab Storage, ADMIN): customer storage counted and quota handed out, top 25 accounts, size distribution, growth (daily snapshot), what customers store (deduped per account) vs raw table totals, the asset library by status (staging = pending checks / held, published, removed) and tier (proprietary SFX library, customer contributions) plus motion/effects kinds, directories / backups / dumps and disks / ZFS pools (live statfs of `/` and `/tank` + the nightly `scripts/cyrus/storage-report.sh` report incl. node-2), estimated disk cost (`cyrus_storage_disk_cost_usd_gb_month`, editable there), add-on run rate and 30-day revenue, quota breaches, alerts (pools at `cyrus_storage_pool_warn_pct` / `_crit_pct`, breaches with no grace, failed renewals); CSV export `/api/admin/cyrus/storage?kind=summary|accounts` (audited, formula-safe). Screenshots `impl-shots/storage-*.png` (fixture data).

''')
ins('docs/cyrus/07-operations.md','## Cloudflare for the Nxeon zones (groundwork only)','''## Storage report and alerts (r51, NOT installed)
`scripts/cyrus/storage-report.sh` (read only: `df`, `zpool list`, `du` of Cyrus' directories and backups on the primary and on node-2 over ssh) writes `CYRUS_STORAGE_REPORT` (default `/var/lib/cyrus/storage-report.json`) for the admin Storage tab; nightly via `deploy/cyrus/cyrus-storage-report.{service,timer}` (idle IO, du over `/tank/backup` takes minutes). `scripts/cyrus/alert-check.sh` has a `disk` rule kind; `deploy/cyrus/alert-rules.json` adds `/` and `/tank` on both hosts (80/90 %) and accounts over quota with no grace. Dry-run verified on node-2.

## Cyrus admin host (r51)
**Today** the Cyrus admin lives inside the Nxeon admin: `/admin/cyrus` on the Nxeon admin host. **After** (owner applies `deploy/cyrus/CYRUS-ADMIN-HOST.md`): the same pages on a secret `<label>.cyrus.my` (`CYRUS_ADMIN_HOST`, label 16-63 `[a-z0-9]`), slim Cyrus chrome, staff only (Nxeon RBAC + 2FA rule + `allowed_admin_ips` via the admin layout, each tab's role area via the host seam), `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` on every answer, 404 for every other path there and for `/admin` on the public Cyrus hosts; optional `CYRUS_ADMIN_IPS`; `CYRUS_ADMIN_HOST_ONLY=1` removes it from the Nxeon admin. nginx template `deploy/cyrus/nginx-cyrus-admin.conf.template`; DNS plan, Cloudflare Access, certificate rule (no per-host Let's Encrypt certificate: CT logs publish names) and the rotation procedure in the plan file. The hostname is a secret: environment only. Before relying on `CYRUS_ADMIN_IPS`, confirm port 3000 is not reachable from outside (it listened on 0.0.0.0 on 2026-10-11).

''')
EOF

## Unverified / known gaps
1. **No real Minecraft client has loaded a pack, texture, sound, model, HUD, menu or creature.** All (T) items in the master plan are unverified.
2. **No paid model build has run** for texture / sound / datapack / import / designer / meshgen specs; AI output quality and token costs are estimates. Eval harness is ready, unrun.
3. Designer behaviour (clicks, projectiles, loot, menus, quests) verified by RCON/log on 1.21.11 and 26.2 only; other versions have no javac classpath. Playtest bots verified on 1.21.11 only; Server D
4. Creature look/animation unverified in a client (BetterModel limits undocumented); creature hand-off with real BetterModel in a full build unrun; Model Studio layer 1/3 UIs follow unreviewed mockups
5. Layer-3 meshes have no export target; meshgen glbs unwrap per part (shared UV texels); meshgen has no real model call, LODs, in-engine load, kernel-escape test or isolated worker.
## Open owner decisions
1. Move-day set: separate Stripe account vs Nxeon as payment provider (default Nxeon), SSO from Nxeon vs Cyrus accounts (default Nxeon IdP), cyrus.my cookie scope and `/mods/cyrus` SEO redirects, wher
2. Config studio ungated? (recommended yes.)
3. AI tagging: tier and cap (about 146k input + 112k output tokens for about 27k leftovers; recommend only the about 4.5k non-sprite assets, skip sprites; thumbnails first).

**Decisions (defaults are placeholders, change in Audit & settings, group Storage):**
1. **Pricing rule (ASSUMPTION, please confirm)**: your per-GB rates read literally have cliffs (24 GB $18.00 > 25 GB $15.00; 49 GB $29.40 > 50 GB $15.00; 99 GB $29.70 > 100 GB $20.00). Implemented default `capped`: the band rate applies (1-4, 5-24, 25-49, 50-99, 100+ GB) and the price is never higher than the next breakpoint: cost(n) = min(rate(n) x n, min over higher breakpoints b of rate(b) x b). Result: 1 GB $0.85, 4 $3.40, 5 $3.75, 10 $7.50, 19 $14.25, **20-50 GB all $15.00**, 60 $18.00, 66 $19.80, **67-100 GB all $20.00**, 150 $30.00, 500 $100.00 (the slider then says "50 GB also costs $15.00").
